questions.q: In 2022, the population of the Philippines grew by what percentage?

questions.e: Population growth was +1.3%, or 1.5 million individuals.

questions.q: Roughly what fraction of eligible people aged 13 and above use social media worldwide?
questions.e: Data suggests roughly three-quarters of people who can use social media do so.

questions.q: What is social media?
o: A platform where machines and users interact to share data and information
questions.e: Social media enables interaction and information sharing.

questions.q: Facebook and LinkedIn are examples of which social media form?
questions.e: Social networking sites focus on connecting people.

questions.q: What is the purpose of forums and message boards?
o: Allowing visitors to interact with opinions, advice, and help
questions.e: Forums let people exchange opinions and help.

questions.q: Microblogging limits posts to roughly how many characters?
questions.e: Microblogging usually allows 160 to 280 characters.

questions.q: Which platform is the classic example of microblogging?
questions.e: Twitter is the lesson's microblogging example.

questions.q: Medium and Tumblr are examples of which social media form?
questions.e: Blogging sites include Medium and Tumblr.

questions.q: Digg, Mix, and Pinterest are examples of which form?
questions.e: Bookmarking sites save and organize links.

questions.q: YouTube and Instagram are examples of which social media form?
questions.e: Media sharing sites let users share photos and videos.

questions.q: Which social media form is considered the most casual and focuses on socializing with friends?
questions.e: Social networking is described as a casual form for socializing.

questions.q: Which form allows users to upload quick thoughts from a phone to a device for others to see?
questions.e: Microblogging is a cousin of texting for quick thoughts.

questions.q: Which platform do Gen Z users trust most for accurate information among the listed sources?
questions.e: Gen Z trust in YouTube was 67%, the highest listed.

questions.q: What percentage of Gen Z users trust YouTube for accurate information?
questions.e: The chart shows 67% for Gen Z on YouTube.

questions.q: Which generation trusts Twitter more for accurate information?
questions.e: Millennials trusted Twitter at 58% versus Gen Z at 36%.

questions.q: Which statement about trust in Facebook is supported by the data?
o: Millennials trust Facebook more than Gen Z
Gen Z trusts Facebook more than Millennials

questions.q: What does the lesson say about Filipino trust in traditional media versus social media?
o: Traditional media is more trusted than social media
Social media is always trusted more
questions.e: TV, radio, and newspapers remain more trusted than social media sites.

questions.q: What percentage of Filipinos were said to have access to social media?
questions.e: Only 49% of Filipinos were said to have social media access.

questions.q: Which mobile generation was implemented from 1987 to 1991?
questions.e: 1G was implemented from 1987 to 1991.

questions.q: What was the primary limitation of 1G?
questions.e: 1G handled voice only.

questions.q: Why was 1G described as analog?
o: It worked like a voice call network
questions.e: 1G was analog, similar to a voice call network.

questions.q: Which issues were encountered with 1G?
o: Poor voice quality and absence of security
questions.e: 1G had poor voice quality and no security.

questions.q: Which device is associated with the 1G era?
questions.e: 1G used brick phones.

questions.q: What small chip was introduced during the 1G era?
questions.e: SIM cards were introduced, a small single chip.

questions.q: Which generation was implemented from 1991 to 2001?
questions.e: 2G ran from 1991 to 2001.

questions.q: What was the main technology used by 2G?
questions.e: 2G relied on GSM.

questions.q: Which messaging services became possible with 2G?
questions.e: 2G enabled SMS and later MMS.

questions.q: Which best describes 2G calls compared with 1G?
questions.e: 2G provided encrypted, clearer digital calls.

questions.q: Which generation was implemented from 2001 to 2009?
questions.e: 3G ran from 2001 to 2009.

questions.q: How much faster was 3G data transfer compared with 2G?
questions.e: 3G was four times faster than 2G.

questions.q: Which capability did 3G enable?
o: Media streaming and large data transfer
questions.e: 3G enabled streaming and large data transfers.

questions.q: What did 3G power according to the lesson?
questions.e: 3G powered modern smartphones and broader device access.

questions.q: According to the speed comparison chart, what was the approximate speed of 1G?
questions.e: 1G speed was about 2.4 Kb/s.

questions.q: According to the chart, what was the approximate speed of 3G?
questions.e: 3G was about 2 Mb/s.

questions.q: According to the chart, what was the approximate speed of 4G?
questions.e: 4G was about 100 Mb/s.

questions.q: According to the chart, what was the approximate speed of 5G?
questions.e: 5G exceeds 1 Gb/s in the comparison chart.

questions.q: When did 5G begin to be presented according to the lesson?
questions.e: 5G is introduced as 2019 and beyond.

questions.q: How much faster than 4G is 5G expected to be?
questions.e: 5G is expected to be 10 to 100 times faster than 4G.

questions.q: What peak speed is 5G expected to reach?
questions.e: 5G speed is expected to clock at 20 Gb/s.

questions.q: Downloading a 5 GB DVD at 50 MB/s takes about 13 minutes. At 5G speed, about how long does it take?
questions.e: The lesson compares 13 minutes with only 2 seconds on 5G.

questions.q: Which is NOT listed as a 5G goal?
questions.e: 5G goals focus on broadband, transformation, IoT, and flexibility.

questions.q: How much capacity do 5G networks promise compared with earlier networks?
questions.e: 5G promises a 1,000-fold capacity gain.

questions.q: Which companies are given as examples working on autonomous driving?
questions.e: Tesla, Alphabet, and Waymo are cited for autonomous driving.

questions.q: Which feature is part of autonomous driving systems?
questions.e: Automated braking and lane changing rely on data capture and analytics.

questions.q: What is edge computing?
o: Storing all data only in a distant data center
Bringing data storage and computation closer to the business or data source
questions.e: Edge computing moves computation and storage closer to the source.

questions.q: Which is a stated advantage of edge computing?
o: Improves response times and saves bandwidth
Requires sending all data to the cloud
questions.e: Edge computing improves response times and saves bandwidth.

questions.q: How does edge computing help with privacy and data sovereignty?
o: It keeps data local, addressing local compliance concerns
It moves data to another country
questions.e: Local processing helps address compliance and sovereignty issues.

questions.q: Why does edge computing reduce costs?
o: It categorizes data locally and reduces the need to retain everything centrally
questions.e: Local categorization reduces bandwidth and redundant storage costs.

questions.q: What is fueling the rapid evolution of edge computing?
o: The Internet of Things and distributed cloud services
questions.e: IoT and distributed cloud drive edge computing.

questions.q: Which four other trends are mentioned but not discussed in detail?
o: 5G, autonomous driving, edge computing, and IoT
Human augmentation, distributed cloud, AI products, and medical upgrade/3D printing
questions.e: The lesson lists these four as other emerging trends.
